lines.raw: The idea in one sentence.
lines.say: The idea in one sentence.

lines.raw: The **MMR** (Monthly Membership Report) is CMS's monthly statement to an MA plan: which members it is paying for, their key status flags, the risk score used, and the amount paid, plus corrections to earlier months.
lines.say: The M M R (Monthly Membership Report) is CMS's monthly statement to an M A plan: which members it is paying for, their key status flags, the risk score used, and the amount paid, plus corrections to earlier months.

lines.raw: How CMS pays an MA plan, in one line.
lines.say: How C M S pays an M A plan, in one line.

scenes.section: How CMS pays an MA plan, in one line

lines.raw: CMS pays the plan a fixed amount **every month for every member**, whether the member visits a doctor or not, and pays more for members with a higher **risk score**.
lines.say: C M S pays the plan a fixed amount every month for every member, whether the member visits a doctor or not, and pays more for members with a higher risk score.

lines.raw: How risk scores and payments are built is taught in the Risk Adjustment course; here we only need the simplified formula to check the MMR.
lines.say: How risk scores and payments are built is taught in the Risk Adjustment course; here we only need the simplified formula to check the M M R.

scenes.section: How CMS pays an MA plan, in one line

lines.raw: The core idea (greatly simplified).
lines.say: The core idea (greatly simplified).

lines.raw: Monthly payment ≈ Base rate times Risk score.
lines.say: Monthly payment ≈ Base rate times Risk score.

lines.raw: For example: Illustrative numbers: base rate $1,100 times Robert's risk score 1.150 equals $1,265.00 per month.
lines.say: For example: Illustrative numbers: base rate 1100 dollars times Robert's risk score 1.150 equals 1265 dollars per month.

lines.raw: Real payments also depend on the plan's bid, rebates, county rates, coding adjustments and more.
lines.say: Real payments also depend on the plan's bid, rebates, county rates, coding adjustments and more.

scenes.section: What is on an MMR row

lines.raw: Risk score.
lines.say: Risk score.

lines.raw: A number around **1.0** for an average beneficiary.
lines.say: A number around 1.0 for an average beneficiary.

lines.raw: 1.150 means "expected to cost about 15% more than average".
lines.say: 1.150 means "expected to cost about 15 percent more than average".

lines.raw: Run month.
lines.say: Run month.

lines.raw: The month CMS produced the report.
lines.say: The month C M S produced the report.

lines.raw: Payment month.
lines.say: Payment month.

lines.raw: The month of coverage the money is for.
lines.say: The month of coverage the money is for.

lines.raw: Usually the same as the run month, but a correction can pay for **earlier** months.
lines.say: Usually the same as the run month, but a correction can pay for earlier months.

lines.raw: Retroactive adjustment.
lines.say: Retroactive adjustment.

lines.raw: A row that corrects money already paid for past months, for example after a risk score update or a late enrollment change.
lines.say: A row that corrects money already paid for past months, for example after a risk score update or a late enrollment change.

lines.raw: Status flags.
lines.say: Status flags.

lines.raw: Yes/no markers such as **ESRD** (end-stage renal disease, kidney failure), **hospice**, **Medicaid** (also on Medicaid) and **institutional** (lives in a nursing home).
lines.say: Yes/no markers such as E S R D (end-stage renal disease, kidney failure), hospice, Medicaid (also on Medicaid) and institutional (lives in a nursing home).

lines.raw: Each one changes how CMS pays for that member.
lines.say: Each one changes how C M S pays for that member.

lines.say: The July run has two rows: the normal July payment, and a correction for January to June.

lines.say: Worked example: checking the mid-year adjustment.

scenes.section: Worked example: checking the mid-year adjustment

lines.raw: Checking the mid-year adjustment.
lines.say: Checking the mid-year adjustment.

lines.raw: New payment − old payment equals $1,100 times 1.180 − $1,100 times 1.150 equals $1,298.00 − $1,265.00 equals $33.00 per month.
lines.say: New payment − old payment equals 1100 dollars times 1.180 − 1100 dollars times 1.150 equals 1298 dollars − 1265 dollars equals 33 dollars per month.

lines.raw: For example: $33.00 times 6 months (January to June) equals $198.00, paid as a retroactive adjustment.
lines.say: For example: 33 dollars times 6 months (January to June) equals 198 dollars, paid as a retroactive adjustment.

lines.raw: Around mid-year CMS updates risk scores with more complete prior-year data, and again in a final update after the year.
lines.say: Around mid-year C M S updates risk scores with more complete prior-year data, and again in a final update after the year.

scenes.section: Worked example: checking the mid-year adjustment

lines.say: Count money by payment month, not run month.

lines.say: If you total the July run, Robert looks like he cost C M S 1496 dollars in July.

lines.raw: In fact $198 of that belongs to January to June.
lines.say: In fact 198 dollars of that belongs to January to June.

lines.say: Group by payment month to see what each month really cost, and by run month only to match the cash C M S sent.

lines.say: Reconciling the M M R.

lines.raw: The plan keeps its own enrollment list.
lines.say: The plan keeps its own enrollment list.

lines.raw: Every month an analyst matches it against the MMR, member by member, using the MBI.
lines.say: Every month an analyst matches it against the M M R, member by member, using the M B I.

lines.raw: Any mismatch can mean money the plan is owed, or money it may have to pay back.
lines.say: Any mismatch can mean money the plan is owed, or money it may have to pay back.

lines.raw: March 2025 reconciliation (three fictional members).
lines.say: March 2025 reconciliation (three fictional members).

lines.raw: 3TW7HC2AP58 (Robert). Plan enrollment list: Enrolled. MMR for March: Paid $1,265.00. What the analyst does: Match: nothing to do.

lines.raw: 5PL2XK8TM14. Plan enrollment list: Enrolled from 1 March. MMR for March: No row. What the analyst does: Check the enrollment was sent and accepted; expect a retro payment in a later run.
lines.say: 5 P L 2 X K 8 T M 1 4. Plan enrollment list: Enrolled from 1 March. M M R for March: No row. What the analyst does: Check the enrollment was sent and accepted; expect a retro payment in a later run.

lines.raw: Why the MMR matters for data.
lines.say: Why the M M R matters for data.

lines.raw: The MMR is the **money and membership truth** from CMS.
lines.say: The M M R is the money and membership truth from C M S.

lines.raw: Finance uses it to book revenue, and analysts use it to count members and to spot members the plan is not being paid for.
lines.say: Finance uses it to book revenue, and analysts use it to count members and to spot members the plan is not being paid for.

lines.say: Diagnoses and risk-score detail come from the M O R and M A O 004, in the next lesson.

lines.raw: Key takeaways.
lines.say: Key takeaways.

lines.raw: The **MMR** is CMS's monthly statement to an MA plan: members, status flags, risk scores and payments.
lines.say: The M M R is CMS's monthly statement to an M A plan: members, status flags, risk scores and payments.

lines.raw: CMS pays roughly **base rate × risk score** per member per month; the Risk Adjustment course explains how scores are built.
lines.say: C M S pays roughly base rate × risk score per member per month; the Risk Adjustment course explains how scores are built.

lines.raw: Retroactive adjustments pay or take back money for **earlier** months; group by payment month to see what each month cost.
lines.say: Retroactive adjustments pay or take back money for earlier months; group by payment month to see what each month cost.

lines.raw: Status flags (ESRD, hospice, Medicaid, institutional) change how a member is paid.
lines.say: Status flags (E S R D, hospice, Medicaid, institutional) change how a member is paid.

lines.raw: Reconcile the MMR against the plan's enrollment list every month, member by member, using the MBI.
lines.say: Reconcile the M M R against the plan's enrollment list every month, member by member, using the M B I.
